chunks: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masroor (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Al-Hussein ibn Muhammad ibn A'mir, from al-Mu'alla ibn Muhammad al-Basri, from Ali ibn Ribat, who said: I said to Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon them both)

that there is a man among us who says that your father (peace be upon him) is alive and that you know about this as you know. He (peace be upon him) said: Glory be to God! The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) died and Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) did not die? Yes, by God, he indeed died, and his property was divided and his slave-wives were married off.
ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali al-Rida confirm the death of his father Imam Musa al-Kazim?
ai.summary: Imam Ali al-Rida (AS) refutes the *Gharibah* (strange/obscure) claim of his father Imam Musa al-Kazim's continued life (*Baqa'*) by citing tangible legal proofs: the distribution of his inheritance (*mirath*) and the marriage of his concubines (*radhiyyat*), which are incompatible with a living person. This narration is pivotal in Shia scholarship for distinguishing between the Imam's physical death and the later doctrine of his occultation (*Ghaybah*), establishing that his death was a historical reality recognized by the community.
